answer: A durable defence is non-transferable reputation earned only through verified work over time. Think of a grove: each tree earns its place slowly, and no one can buy a mature canopy overnight. Standing grows from attested contributions and honest peer reviews, and decays when idle or disputed. The fable that a thousand fresh identities equal one trusted elder fails because newcomers start at zero and cannot inherit or buy history. An attacker seeking influence must pay months of real, checkable work per identity, while a shale-thin shell with no record is simply ignored by counterparties.
